text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Fokker workers delegation delivers open letter to Stork accusing the group of stalling the restart of the bankrupt aircraft maker. (p1)
- Creating shareholder value gains importance among managers of Dutch companies. (p1)
- Friesland Bank buys a 60 percent stake in Amsterdam stockbroker Bangert-Pontier. (p1)
- Record number of Dutch corporate owner-directors became tax exiles in Belgium during last few months of 1996. (p1)
- Trading house Geveke boosts 1996 net by 18 percent; company's orderbooks give hope for the future. (p3)
- LCI Computer Group forecasts continued profit growth. (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines KLM's financial director optimistic about chance of a new form of co-operation between KLM and Northwest Airlines. (p3)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT takes over Britain's computer wholesaler Simons Magee. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch trade surplus in first eleven months of 1996 six billion guilders higher than in same period of 1995. (p2)
- Food and detergent group Unilever in conflict with rival margarine plant Brinkers over margarine marketing. (p2)
- President of Germany's central bank Hans Tietmeyer supports Wim Duisenberg as European central bank head. (p2)
- Meat factory Dumeco closes one of its pig slaughter houses due to swine fever. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg nominated European banker of the year. (p1)
- Euro-MP of the Green party leaks confidential EU documents on the Internet. (p9)
- Automation company Triple P posts 2.5 million guilders losses in 1996 vs 10.5 million guilder profit in 1995. (p21)
- ABN AMRO bank buys futures market activities of Citicorp. (p21)
TROUW
- Unrest in building sector is growing amid lack of new pay and conditions agreement. (p7)
- Utrech/Amsterdam energy company Una gives up its resistance to merger plans of four large energy producers. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Spain's junior foreign affairs minister De Miguel calls the Netherlands' EU chairmanship weak. (p1)
- Dutch PTT Telecom seems to miss chance of moving into South Africa. (p13)
